problem_statement: RIOT must provide a compile-time, machine-readable version identifier that can be used in C and preprocessor checks. Provide a macro RIOT_VERSION_NUM(major, minor, patch, extra) that returns a 64-bit integer with the four arguments packed into consecutive 16-bit fields, major most significant and extra least significant, so the original values can be recovered by standard 16-bit shifts and masks. Also make RIOT_VERSION_CODE available to compiled code as a value of the same form representing the RIOT version being built, so it can be compared with RIOT_VERSION_NUM(...) and used in preprocessor conditionals.

verification.reason: The statement is mostly complete, but it omits the public header location, the preprocessor-macro requirement, and the CI-build availability requirement that the hidden tests rely on. These can be added without revealing the implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden test includes kernel_defines.h and expects RIOT_VERSION_NUM to be visible there, but the statement does not name the header or state that the macro must be provided by it.

The hidden test uses RIOT_VERSION_CODE and RIOT_VERSION_NUM in preprocessor #if expressions, requiring them to be usable as preprocessor integer expressions; the statement only says RIOT_VERSION_CODE is available to compiled code.
The fix ensures RIOT_VERSION_CODE is defined even in CI builds where RIOT_VERSION may be a non-numeric placeholder; the statement does not mention this configuration/edge case.

problem_statement_fixed: RIOT must provide a compile-time, machine-readable version identifier that can be used in C and preprocessor checks. Provide a macro RIOT_VERSION_NUM(major, minor, patch, extra) in core/include/kernel_defines.h that returns a 64-bit integer with the four arguments packed into consecutive 16-bit fields, major most significant and extra least significant, so the original values can be recovered by standard 16-bit shifts and masks. The macro must be usable in preprocessor conditionals. Also make RIOT_VERSION_CODE available to compiled code and to the preprocessor as a macro of the same form representing the RIOT version being built, so it can be compared with RIOT_VERSION_NUM(...).
